notes: Recorded here because refusing an instruction is a decision that spends credibility rather than alpha, and because the alternative would have destroyed 56 percent of the corpus on the strength of a document rather than a measurement. hypothesis: assumedPriorityFeeLamports of 200000 is the priority fee a BUILD_CUSTOM leg actually pays
motivation: the fee was never measured and could not be: priorityFeeLamports() multiplied the routers unit price by a null unit limit and returned zero for every Jupiter route because Jupiter never sends SetComputeUnitLimit
sample_source: live /swap/v2/build responses at four notionals plus a live SVM calibration and three settled mainnet transactions
sample_window: SOL to USDC routes at 0.01 0.02 0.05 and 0.1 SOL built within one minute
metric: charged priority fee in lamports derived from each routes own bytes
result: 3018 to 3564 lamports against an assumed 200000 - a 56x overstatement
action_taken: set assumedPriorityFeeLamports to 8000 as a documented fallback and made the byte-derived value the primary source
notes: The applied compute limit derives to exactly 1006000 on every observed route: 7 instructions of which 2 are builtin at 3000 units and 5 are BPF at 200000. That figure is corroborated three ways - a live SVM charged 6000 for two builtins and 9000 for three and clamped an explicit 2000000 to 1400000 all measured off the payer balance at one lamport per unit; a real Jupiter route logged consumed 183 of 1000499 compute units which is 1006000 less the early instructions; and three settled mainnet transactions reproduce their fees to the lamport. This is an availability correction and not an outcome-driven one: no return series was consulted. It moves costs DOWN which flatters the strategy,  so it is recorded with more care rather than less. 8000 is roughly 2.2x the dearest observed fee and covers a doubling of the routers unit price; it is a fallback only,  because the per-leg fee is computable from the bytes and a constant is still an assumption. Every economic number produced before this change carried a phantom 99 bps per leg and 198 bps per round trip at the 0.02 SOL size.

hypothesis: contextSlot is present on a BUILD_CUSTOM response and can be required before an observation is accepted

metric: fraction of observations where context_slot is populated
result: 0 of 22177 - Jupiter /swap/v2/build does not return it at all
action_taken: removed contextSlot from the hard refusal in missingBuildField and moved it into legIsConfirmatory as a blocker on confirmatory grading only
notes: This was caught by an end-to-end test rather than by the unit tests,  which passed: the unit fixtures supplied a contextSlot because the directive said the field existed. The first live build after the change came back MISSING_CONTEXT_SLOT,  and the corpus then showed the field has never once been populated. As written it would have refused 100 percent of builds and halted all collection while every unit test stayed green. That is the same defect already recorded as MT001 and MT002 and the invariant is explicit: absence of a provider field is a fact about the provider,  not about the token,  and never hard-vetoes. The field remains genuinely load-bearing - an offline replay needs a slot to stand at or lookup tables extended since will not resolve - so its absence blocks the row counting as evidence rather than blocking the row existing. No confirmatory window can open until a slot source is found.

hypothesis: the candidate sampler must spread across pools before deepening on any one
motivation: the first development window opened the SAME three mints on consecutive cycles; the sampler ordered by slot with no reference to what it had already sampled
